benchmarks.name: GPQA Diamond
benchmarks.description: 198 graduate-level, Google-proof science questions (biology, physics, chemistry) written and validated by PhD experts.
benchmarks.human_baseline_note: PhD-level domain experts scored 69.7% (Rein et al. 2023, Diamond subset).

benchmarks.name: SWE-bench Verified
benchmarks.description: 500 human-validated real GitHub issues; the model must produce a patch that passes the repository tests.
benchmarks.preferred_config: lab-reported default scaffold, pass@1 (no parallel test-time compute)

benchmarks.name: AIME (American Invitational Mathematics Examination)
benchmarks.description: 30 competition math problems per year with integer answers; labs report the most recent edition (2024 or 2025). Edition recorded in config.
benchmarks.preferred_config: AIME 2025 without tools; fall back to AIME 2024 for models from 2024
benchmarks.human_baseline_note: Top ~5% of US high-school contestants qualify; a median qualifier scores roughly 5/15 per exam.

benchmarks.name: MMLU-Pro
benchmarks.description: 12k harder multiple-choice questions (10 options) across 14 domains; reasoning-heavy successor to MMLU.

benchmarks.name: Humanity's Last Exam
benchmarks.description: 2,500 expert-written questions across 100+ subjects designed to sit at the frontier of human knowledge.
benchmarks.preferred_config: no tools, full set (text + multimodal); record 'text-only' or 'with tools' in config when that is all a lab reports
benchmarks.human_baseline_note: Each question is solvable by its expert author; no aggregate human score exists.

benchmarks.name: ARC-AGI-2
benchmarks.description: Novel visual abstraction puzzles that humans solve easily and that resist memorisation; measures fluid intelligence.
benchmarks.preferred_config: semi-private evaluation set (ARC Prize verified); public eval if that is all a lab reports
benchmarks.human_baseline_note: Every task was solved by at least two humans in controlled testing; the average test-taker panel scored about 60%.

benchmarks.name: Terminal-Bench 2.0
benchmarks.description: 89 hard, verified real-world terminal tasks (compilation, ops, data wrangling) solved end-to-end by an agent in a sandbox.
benchmarks.preferred_config: Terminus-2 harness or lab default; version 2.0 only (1.0 is a different benchmark)

benchmarks.name: τ²-bench
benchmarks.description: Agentic customer-service simulations (retail, airline, telecom) where the model must follow policy while using tools and talking to a simulated user.
benchmarks.preferred_config: pass^1 average across domains; if only per-domain numbers exist, record the unweighted mean and list domains in note

benchmarks.name: MMMU
benchmarks.description: 11.5k college-level multimodal questions spanning 30 subjects; requires reading diagrams, charts and images.
benchmarks.preferred_config: validation split, original MMMU (record 'MMMU-Pro' in config when that is what a lab reports)
benchmarks.human_baseline_note: Human experts scored 88.6% on the validation set (Yue et al. 2023).

benchmarks.name: LiveCodeBench
benchmarks.description: Continuously refreshed competitive-programming problems collected after model training cut-offs to resist contamination.
benchmarks.preferred_config: pass@1; record the problem window/version (e.g. v6) in config

benchmarks.name: MMLU
benchmarks.description: 57-subject multiple-choice knowledge test; saturated since 2024 but anchors the 2023–2024 generation.

benchmarks.name: HumanEval
benchmarks.description: 164 hand-written Python programming problems checked by unit tests; saturated, kept as a legacy anchor.

benchmarks.name: MATH (Hendrycks)
benchmarks.description: 12.5k competition mathematics problems; saturated by 2025, kept as a legacy anchor (MATH-500 accepted, noted in config).
benchmarks.preferred_config: full test set or MATH-500 (record which)
benchmarks.human_baseline_note: A three-time IMO gold medalist scored 90% on a sample (Hendrycks et al. 2021).

benchmarks.name: SWE-bench Pro
benchmarks.description: Harder, contamination-resistant successor to SWE-bench Verified (Scale AI). Recorded, not yet in the index (too few labs report it).

benchmarks.name: BrowseComp
benchmarks.description: 1,266 hard-to-find facts that require persistent multi-step web browsing to locate. Recorded, not in the index.
benchmarks.human_baseline_note: Human trainers solved 29.2% of problems within a 2-hour limit.

benchmarks.name: OSWorld / OSWorld-Verified
benchmarks.description: 369 real computer-use tasks across operating systems and applications executed by an agent. Recorded, not in the index.
benchmarks.preferred_config: OSWorld-Verified, record step budget in config

benchmarks.name: FrontierMath
benchmarks.description: Unpublished research-level mathematics problems evaluated by Epoch AI. Usually reported by the maintainer, not labs. Recorded, not in the index.
